forecast-period.text: Over the weekend, a high pressure system to the south of SA is forecast to continue extending a ridge across the state, as it moves slowly east, to be centred over Victoria by Monday. A cold front is then forecast to move across the state on Tuesday, as another ridge pushes in behind the front.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Morning fog patches about the southern coastal districts. Dry, apart from a slight chance of a shower near the western border. Maximum temperatures above average. East to southeasterly winds, fresh at times during the afternoon in the northeast. Winds tending southerly in the southeast.

Morning fog on and east of the ranges, with patchy frost possible about the South East districts. Dry and mostly sunny day. Maximum temperatures above average. East to southeasterly winds, fresh at times during the afternoon in the northeast. Winds tending northeasterly about the west and southerly in the southeast.

Morning fog and frost patches on and east of the ranges, as well as possible fog about the Eyre Peninsula. Dry and mostly sunny day. Warmer, with above average maximum temperatures. North to northeasterly winds, tending easterly in the northeast.

text.p: Isolated showers developing about the Agricultural Areas during the day. Maximum temperatures generally above average. North to northwesterly winds, freshening at times about the coastal fringe and the ranges, ahead of a west to southwesterly change extending across the state throughout the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Tuesday: 2 to 5 mm in the far west and Agricultural Areas, mainly about windward coasts and ranges, and in the South East, with local falls of 5 to 15 mm possible. Isolated falls of 15 to 30 mm are possible near the western border with thunderstorms.
